description:
Here are the descriptions of the line plots, following your guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. 

A blue line, marked with square symbols and error bars, represents “Final Accuracy”. It begins at approximately 0.82 with an accuracy of 0.83 and ends at approximately 0.99 with an accuracy of 0.86. The line generally fluctuates between 0.83 and 0.88 throughout the x-axis range. An orange line, marked with circle symbols and error bars, represents “Δ Accuracy”. It starts at approximately 0.81 with an accuracy of 0.45 and ends at approximately 0.99 with an accuracy of 0.08. This line shows a general decline in accuracy across the x-axis range. A green line, marked with triangle symbols and error bars, represents “Initial Accuracy”. It begins at approximately 0.81 with an accuracy of 0.45 and ends at approximately 0.99 with an accuracy of 0.86. This line generally increases in accuracy across the x-axis range.
